title: Dispatch: Fix campaign-rule temporal semantics, seam typing, and test gaps (attempt 2)
description:
Dispatch of eshyra-jhpt.2 (attempt 2) — supervisor review fixes on top of attempt 1.

Attempt 1 (eshyra-jhpt.2.1, commit 87e7587) is largely sound and is KEPT: migration 0025 with its CHECK constraints mirroring the domain unions, the lossless provenance columns, the jsonColumn use, the SQL ordering that leans on the self-sorting position encoding, the storage-side revoked_position decision (accepted — it is storage state, and eshyra-jhpt.5 can read revocation history from it), and the migrationLegacyAdoption.test.ts ledger updates (mandatory, correct). Do not revert any of that. Supervisor review found six defects; two are severe and reproduced below.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.2.2 on branch eshyra-jhpt.2.2, cut from 87e7587 on eshyra-jhpt.2.1 so attempt 1's work is present. Work only inside that worktree.

FINDING 1 (SEVERE) — rulings and house rules use DIFFERENT temporal semantics, so they disagree at any historical or replay position.
activeRows(db, campaignId, cutoff) has two unrelated behaviours. With a cutoff it applies correct HISTORICAL semantics (effective_position <= cutoff, not-yet-revoked at cutoff, not-yet-superseded at cutoff). Without a cutoff it applies `status = 'active'` only. createCampaignRuleReadSeam then calls activeRows WITH the caller's position for house rules, but activeRulingsForAmbiguities calls activeRows(db, campaignId) with NO cutoff — so rulings are answered with current-status semantics no matter which position is being asked about.

Reproduced (supervisor probe, both rules created effective at ordinal 1 and superseded at ordinal 10, then queried at replay position 5):
    house rules at replay position 5 : [ 'h-old' ]   <- historical semantics, correct
    rulings    at replay position 5 : [ 'r-new' ]   <- current-status semantics, WRONG

At position 5 the active ruling was r-old. This breaks the epic's central scenarios: eshyra-jhpt.4 requires DM and auditor to receive equivalent active sets at the turn's effective position, and eshyra-jhpt.8 replays a disputed turn under the rules active at that turn. A ruling superseded after the disputed turn is silently replaced by its successor during replay, while an equivalent house rule is handled correctly.
FIX: one temporal predicate for both kinds. The seam interface cannot take a position on activeRulingsForAmbiguities, so bind it at construction: give createCampaignRuleReadSeam an optional campaign position that activeRulingsForAmbiguities uses, and make activeRulesAtPosition consistent with it. Also add a direct, position-aware store API for rulings (e.g. listActiveRulingsForAmbiguitiesAtPosition(db, campaignId, ambiguityIds, campaignPosition)) so eshyra-jhpt.4 and .8 can ask for a historical position without going through the position-blind seam signature. Document on the seam factory that the discovery seam is position-blind for rulings by contract and that the bound position is what makes it correct.

FINDING 2 (SEVERE) — the position-less query does not mean "unfiltered", it means "wrong": future-effective rules leak.
With no cutoff the predicate is `status = 'active'` and effective_position is ignored entirely, so a rule that does not take effect until a much later position is returned as active now.
Reproduced (one house rule effective at ordinal 999):
    at position 1 : []
    no position   : [ 'future' ]      <- future rule leaks
eshyra-jhpt.3's acceptance criteria require "all and only rules active at the current campaign position" and explicit prospective/effective-turn filtering; a caller that omits the position gets a semantically different set, not merely a broader one, which also makes DM/auditor divergence easy to introduce in .4.
FIX: give the store ONE temporal semantic. Either make the position required on the active-at-position path, or define the position-less case explicitly as "at the latest recorded position" and implement it that way (still filtering effective_position). Whichever you choose, add a test proving the position-less result equals the result at the latest recorded position, and never returns a rule whose effective position is in the future.

FINDING 3 (test coverage) — the primary seam method's positive path is never exercised, and four required tests are missing.
activeRulingsForAmbiguities can only ever return rulings with 'ambiguity' provenance, but every ruling in the test file is built with 'recurring-question' provenance, so no test creates a rule that method could return. The only assertion, `expect(seam.activeRulingsForAmbiguities(['not-q'])).toEqual([])`, passes vacuously and would still pass if the method returned nothing at all. This is the method eshyra-jhpt.6 and transition probe P7 depend on.
Also missing from the required list on eshyra-jhpt.2.1: checkpoint/restore round trip; cross-campaign isolation; disputed-turn effective positions (every test rule is 'prospective'); invalid supersession combinations.
FIX: add all of them. For the ruling path, create a real ambiguity-provenance ruling (validateCampaignRule requires the ambiguity, so pass it via the validation options — that requirement is correct, keep it) and assert it is returned for its ambiguity id, is not returned for an unrelated id, and is not returned by activeRulesAtPosition. For checkpoint/restore, note that persistence/checkpoint/serialize.ts enumerates tables from sqlite_master so campaign_rule is captured automatically — the test proves the round trip preserves identities, ordering, provenance, statuses, and effective positions; it must not add checkpoint machinery.

FINDING 4 (idiom) — storage errors are plain `Error`.
campaignRuleStore.ts throws `new Error(...)` in six places. The domain module defines CampaignRuleError and the codebase convention is a domain error class per module (campaign.ts CampaignError, itemState.ts ItemStateError, and so on). Callers cannot distinguish a campaign-rule failure from an arbitrary runtime error.
FIX: throw CampaignRuleError (imported from campaignRules.js) from the store.

FINDING 5 (type safety) — nothing proves the seam implementation satisfies the interface.
createCampaignRuleReadSeam has no return type annotation, so its object literal is only structurally typed, and the body uses `as CampaignRuleProjection[]` to force the shape. If the CampaignRuleReadSeam contract changes, this silently stops matching.
FIX: annotate the return type as CampaignRuleReadSeam (import the type from discovery/types.js, which re-exports the campaign-domain projection types) and remove the cast so the compiler checks it. The trailing `.filter((r): r is CampaignRulingProjection => ...)` is unreachable given the ambiguity-provenance filter above it — simplify it or make it a genuine narrowing.

FINDING 6 (validation gaps in the acceptance criteria) — revocation and supersession are not required to be prospective.
revokeCampaignRule accepts any revokedPosition, including one before the rule's own effectivePosition. supersedeCampaignRule does not require the successor's effectivePosition to be at or after the prior rule's, yet the historical predicate relies on the successor's position to decide when the prior stopped being active. Both produce degenerate rules that are never active at any position. "Revoke prospectively" is an explicit acceptance criterion on eshyra-jhpt.2.
FIX: reject a revocation position earlier than the rule's effective position, and reject a successor whose effective position precedes the rule it supersedes. Test both rejections.

SCOPE
Unchanged: storage and query APIs only. No prompt/context assembly (.3/.4), no ambiguity dialogue (.6), no replay orchestration (.8), no CLI (.5). Do not edit packages/core/src/campaign/campaignRules.ts — the eshyra-jhpt.1 domain model is merged and closed; if you believe it must change, file a bd issue and report it instead. Do not fix the discovery-side cast tracked by eshyra-neus.
Add a brief comment where SQL ORDER BY relies on the canonical position encoding being self-sorting, so the dependency is visible if anyone revisits the encoding.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root, BEFORE committing (it rewrites files).
notes:

Completed in commit 75ef96d. Fixed all six review findings: unified historical active-row semantics with latest-recorded-position fallback for omitted cutoffs; added position-aware ruling queries and bound seam position documentation; added ruling, temporal, isolation, invalid lifecycle, and checkpoint/restore coverage; replaced campaign-rule store plain Errors with CampaignRuleError; added CampaignRuleReadSeam return typing and a real ambiguity-ruling type guard; enforced prospective revocation and supersession positions. Adjusted the boundary test to distinguish required type-only imports from runtime discovery imports.
